Cyber Attack Disrupts Indonesian Transportation & Logistics Sector Operations

Jakarta – A major cyber attack targeting Indonesia’s Transportation & Logistics sector has caused widespread disruption to freight movement, warehousing operations, and administrative processes across the country, industry sources confirmed on Tuesday. The incident, first detected late Monday night, is believed to involve a sophisticated ransomware variant that has crippled the IT systems of several leading logistics firms, including PT Nusantara Ekspres and Garuda Logistics Network.

The Indonesian Transportation & Logistics Association (ITLA) warned that the attack is ongoing, with many companies still struggling to regain access to critical platforms used for route management, cargo tracking, and payroll administration. “This is an unprecedented event for our industry,” said ITLA chairperson Irwan Prasetyo. “Key operational systems have been rendered inaccessible, forcing manual workarounds and significant slowdowns at major distribution hubs.”

The attack has affected both urban and regional sites, with some facilities reporting complete shutdowns of warehouse management systems and digital manifests. At PT Nusantara Ekspres’ main depot in Bekasi, trucks sat idle as dispatchers reverted to paper records to release shipments, resulting in lengthy delays. “We are doing our best to keep goods moving, but the process is extremely slow without our usual systems,” said depot manager Siti Handayani.

Thousands of logistics workers have been directly impacted. Many have been temporarily reassigned to manual sorting and inventory checks, while others face uncertainty as digital timekeeping and payroll functions remain offline. “I’ve never seen our team so stretched,” reported Rahmat, a warehouse supervisor at Garuda Logistics Network’s Surabaya facility. “We’re working overtime to process even a fraction of the usual volume.”

Industry analysts estimate that the disruption could take several days to resolve, depending on the ability of firms to restore backups or negotiate with the attackers. “The Transportation & Logistics sector is particularly vulnerable to this kind of attack due to its reliance on integrated IT systems and just-in-time processes,” noted Hana Saputra, a cybersecurity consultant based in Jakarta.

The Ministry of Transportation has called for an urgent review of digital defenses across the sector. “Safeguarding the continuity of logistics operations is critical for Indonesia’s economy,” said Director General Budi Santoso in a statement.

At the time of writing, most affected companies had not received any indication of when their systems might be restored. The ITLA urged all sector operators to remain vigilant and to coordinate closely with authorities as investigation and recovery efforts continue.
